_note: Skeleton for docs/ledger-exemptions.json — the factory's own declaration of which ledger SEQUENCE omissions are excused, read by tools/ledger.py at the point it would report them. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and leave `exempt` EMPTY unless your factory has one, because an entry excuses a real omission. WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A CONSTANT IN THE TOOL: SKILL.md section 11 requires an exemption table to hold its entries as FACTORY DATA in its own file and never inline in the gate, because the tool is paired byte-identically with its template copy and a factory's own history must not ship to every new factory. The ledger tool carried three inline entries until 2026-09-25 — this factory's pre-gate closes of #6 and #8, dated 2026-09-12, with the rulings that granted them — which meant a factory that happened to work on #6 or #8 could have had ITS sequence defects excused by a history that was never its own. Each entry has five REQUIRED fields: `subject` (the work unit, as written in the row), `leg` (which leg's predicate is being excused — `intake` or `claim` for the close sequence, `dispatch` for the work-unit dispatch leg), `granted` (the date the exemption was granted, ISO-8601), `reason` (why the omission happened), and `proof` (the external receipt that admits it — normally the ledger row number of the ruling that granted it). A blank `proof` is REFUSED at the point it would excuse an omission, so an entry nobody could defend in the output is one that gets fixed instead. An exemption is a VISIBLE DEBT, not forgiveness: every entry that MATCHES is printed as an `excused:` line on every run, and the closing line distinguishes clean from excused, so the two are never the same output. An ABSENT file means this factory has declared none, which is the shipped state of a new factory; a file that exists and cannot be READ is a reported problem, because only the silent failure is the hazard. An entry with a blank `proof` loads but excuses nothing — `verify` refuses it by name at the point it would excuse an omission.
